## Analysis Summary

**Test image observations:**
- Subject: corn stalk (cylindrical stem structure, nodal region visible on left)
- Background tissue: tan/golden/straw-colored (mature, dried tissue)
- Key feature: extremely dense, uniformly distributed tiny black dots covering the entire surface
- The dots are very small, uniform in size, and scattered with no pattern/grouping

**Candidate elimination:**
- Leaf diseases (Gray_leaf_spot, Northern_corn_leaf_blight, Eyespot, Tar_spot, etc.): eliminated — test image is stalk tissue, not leaf
- Fusarium, Diplodia_stalk_rot: show fibrous tan pith tissue without the distinctive black dot pattern
- Physoderma_stalk_rot: shows broad dark brown/black node staining, not individual tiny dots
- Anthracnose_stalk_rot: shows larger blotchy black surface discoloration, not uniform tiny dots

**Best match — Charcoal_stalk_rot:**
The hallmark diagnostic feature of charcoal stalk rot (*Macrophomina phaseolina*) is the formation of **microsclerotia** — tiny black spherical bodies (50-150 μm) scattered densely throughout the infected pith tissue. When viewed up close, these produce exactly the "pepper-and-salt" or "charcoal dust" appearance seen in the test image: countless tiny black specks uniformly distributed against a pale/tan straw-colored stalk background. The reference images for Charcoal_stalk_rot confirm the dark gray/charcoal-colored pith interior consistent with massive microsclerotia accumulation.
